articles.title: NFL Monday Night Football preview: Bears, without QB Caleb Williams, try to beat undefeated Eagles
articles.summary: The Eagles are 2-0 after two very close wins to start the season.
articles.body:
The memes over Caleb Williams' reaction to his hamstring injury were funny, but the injury was bad enough to keep the Chicago Bears quarterback out for at least one game.

Williams is developing into one of the NFL's best quarterbacks and now the Bears have to figure out a way to win without him. The Bears will start veteran Case Keenum , Fox Sports' Jay Glazer reported Sunday , with normal backup Tyson Bagent available if needed. Bagent was cleared from concussion protocol but the Bears are reportedly more comfortable with Keenum after Bagent missed most of last week's practices.

Keenum has experience. He has 66 career starts. In 2017, the Vikings were 11-3 in his starts. Keenum is also 38 years old and hasn't taken a regular-season snap since 2023. He has started only four games this decade. It's a big test for Bears coach Ben Johnson, a sharp offensive coach who has to call an NFL game without a No. 1 overall pick at quarterback for the first time.

The Bears will be trying to move the ball against an Eagles defense that has been good again to begin this season, even if it hasn't been great yet. Philadelphia was 12th in points allowed and 10th in yards allowed after two weeks, though only 23rd in EPA ( expected points added ) per play. Last season Philadelphia was ninth in EPA per play. It's a talented defense that should be among the NFL's top 10 again, and could have a big day feasting on an offense down to its third option at quarterback.

The Eagles have started the season 2-0 but needed to stop a late two-point conversion to beat the Commanders in Week 1 and a last-minute drive to win at Tennessee last week. Philadelphia catches a break facing a Bears team without its starting quarterback. We'll see how the Bears offense adjusts without Williams.

It's not like the Eagles have their backs against the wall at 2-0. But this is a game they're expected to win, due to Caleb Williams ' injury. Losing to Case Keenum (or Tyson Bagent, if the Bears have a change of heart) would now become a bad loss for them. The Bears would be thrilled to get a win without their quarterback, but realistically it shouldn't be expected. The pressure goes onto the Eagles for this one.

Key players: Bears RBs D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai

When the Bears scored 59 points in the opener, Caleb Williams got a lot of the credit. And he did play well. But that ignored that Swift had 124 yards rushing and Monangai added 100. They combined for four touchdowns on the ground. The Bears offense didn't do much last week, and Swift lost a critical fumble near the goal line, but they need their running backs to bounce back in a big way this week. It's pretty simple when you're down to a 38-year-old journeyman at quarterback, taking his first regular-season snaps in three years: The Bears need a lot from Swift and Monangai. The Eagles haven't been great against the run yet this season, allowing 4.2 yards per carry (19th in the NFL) and the Bears need to exploit that to win on Monday night.

A ton of line movement in this game, as it was Chicago as a small favorite before Caleb Williams' injury and moved all the way out to Eagles -4.5, before it's come back to -3.5. Even though backup Tyson Bagent cleared concussion protocol, it will reportedly be Case Keenum starting for the Bears. Philadelphia hasn't been particularly impressive, but stands at 2-0, while the Bears can't afford to fall too far behind in a crowded NFC without Williams. The betting public is backing the Eagles, but I'm looking to back another prime-time under (41.5) here. I think Philadelphia's defense shows up and reminds us why Keenum is a third-string QB at this moment in his career.

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

Another whirlwind week of NFL action comes to a close Monday with the Eagles taking on the Bears. Here are three themes to track from a fantasy perspective:

1. Can Chicago fix its passing game with a backup quarterback?

Journeyman Case Keenum steps in for an emergency start, replacing Caleb Williams (out multiple weeks) and Tyson Bagent (probably out one week). Normally this type of news would be a kill shot for any passing game, especially one slumping like Chicago's, but you never want to discount a creative play caller like Ben Johnson. Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland were difficult fantasy calls all week.

2. What version of Saquon Barkley will we see?

Barkley was solid if unspectacular in the season opener, then missed most the Week 2 with a stinger. He's no longer a major factor in the passing game, and this is the worst Philadelphia offensive line he's ever run behind. Still, when healthy, Barkley is a rare bell cow and an automatic fantasy start.

3. How will the Philadelphia passing game adjust without Dallas Goedart?

The veteran tight end has been a touchdown gobbler the last couple of years, but now he's out multiple weeks. DeVonta Smith had a breakout game in Week 2 and Dontayvion Wicks has legitimate sleeper value, especially with more targets now up for grabs.

articles.title: Commanders' Leo Chenal Provides Update After Season-Ending Surgery After Scary Injury vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: Washington Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal revealed that his surgery "went well" after he suffered a neck injury in Sunday's 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal revealed that his surgery "went well" after he suffered a neck injury in Sunday's 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz previously reported Chanel would have season-ending surgery.

Chenal was carted off the field midway through the second quarter. His brother subsequently posted on social media he could move his arms and legs and had no signs of nerve damage.

Chenal is in his first season with Washington after signing a three-year, $24.8 million contract. He had previously played for the Kansas City Chiefs, who selected him in the third round of the 2022 NFL draft.

The 25-year-old appeared in 14 games for Kansas City in 2025, finishing with 58 combined tackles and two sacks.

Chenal came off the bench in Washington's season-opening loss to the Philadelphia Eagles but started over the next two weeks with Frankie Luvu sidelined. Luvu is nursing a groin strain .

The Commanders are also without the services of Jordan Magee, who landed on injured reserve earlier this month.

Chenal was off to a strong start. He had 18 tackles and one tackle for loss through Washington's first three contests.

articles.title: Did Maxx Crosby just put Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs on notice after Raiders’ 3-0 start
articles.summary: Maxx Crosby gave the Las Vegas Raiders enough time to enjoy 3-0. Then he reminded everyone who was coming next.
articles.body: Maxx Crosby gave the Las Vegas Raiders enough time to enjoy 3-0. Then he reminded everyone who was coming next.After Las Vegas beat the New Orleans Saints 35-27 on Sept. 27, Crosby addressed his teammates with an expletive-filled message about Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. Both AFC West teams enter their Week 4 meeting unbeaten.What did Maxx Crosby tell the Raiders about Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs?Crosby did not let the Raiders’ comeback win become an extended celebration.In a locker-room video released after the game, the Raiders defensive end acknowledged the victory before immediately turning toward Kansas City.“It’s a great f***** win, but we got a great f****** team coming into town. We already know what the f***, we already know what it is, bro, it’s the f****** Kansas City Chiefs,”* Crosby said. “Enjoy this s** tonight. Take care of your bodies and we’re f****** on a war path to get what we want, man. Love y’all boys. Let’s get it! Gang on me! Gang on three! 1 2 3, gang!”*Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak delivered the same message with considerably fewer expletives.“Hey, last thing here guys, listen. You’re 3-0 cause’ of the type of people that you are, how hard you work, how much you care about each other, how important it is to you. Okay? So let’s dial it back in. We all know what’s coming into our place, okay?”The timing gives Crosby’s speech some weight.Las Vegas and Kansas City are both 3-0 heading into their Oct. 4 game at Allegiant Stadium. For the Raiders, it is also their first 3-0 start since 2021.Crosby has plenty of history with Mahomes.He explained on “Bussin’ With The Boys” in August that the two have mutual respect away from football. That disappears once they line up against each other.“But like Pat Mahomes, like we go to war. Like we go to f***** war. He knows I’m trying to murder him and that m************ is trying to make me look stupid every time. But off the field, it’s love every time.”*Now Crosby gets Mahomes again with an unbeaten record on the line.Why does the Raiders’ defense make Maxx Crosby’s Chiefs warning worth watching?Crosby’s words came after the Raiders defense gave him some evidence to work with.Las Vegas allowed 27 points through three quarters against New Orleans. The Saints did not score again.According to Athlon Sports’ Tyler Bischoff, the Raiders have allowed zero fourth-quarter points through their first three games this season.Against New Orleans, the defense also forced four turnovers in the fourth quarter.Malcolm Koonce hit Saints quarterback Tyler Shough and forced a fumble that Crosby recovered. Las Vegas converted the turnover into a go-ahead score.Hezekiah Masses later intercepted Shough and returned the ball inside the Saints’ five-yard line. Jeremy Chinn followed with another forced fumble on a fourth-down sack before Nakobe Dean forced the Saints’ final turnover.Eric Stokes recovered that fumble to effectively secure the victory.Those takeaways repeatedly gave Las Vegas short fields. Athlon reported that the Raiders’ average starting field position in the fourth quarter was the Saints’ 40.5-yard line.That matters because the Raiders did not need their offense to manufacture long scoring drives while chasing the game. Their defense kept handing it favorable situations.Crosby also produced one of the biggest plays himself with his fourth-quarter recovery.After the win, he pointed to the Raiders’ locker-room chemistry as one reason for their early success.“We have a great group and guys that love playing football together,” Crosby said, according to Heavy’s Eduardo Razo. “We practice together, we eat together, we talk all the time together. In those big moments, there’s no panic.”Kansas City presents a different test.Crosby has faced Mahomes throughout his Raiders career, and the Chiefs have repeatedly controlled the rivalry. This meeting arrives with both teams undefeated and Las Vegas coming off another fourth-quarter defensive stand.The Raiders celebrated Sunday night. articles.title: Dolphins RB De'Von Achane will reportedly miss the remainder of the season due to torn ACL
articles.summary: Miami will likely add RB depth behind presumed new starter Ollie Gordon.
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a torn ACL, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Achane suffered the injury in the first quarter of Sunday's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs . The running back began the game with three carries for 17 yards. His last touch was a run to the left where Achane picked up 11 yards.

The running back went down after trying to cut back toward the middle of the field. He was able to walk off under his own power and remained on the sideline. It was tough to see at first where the injury occurred because it looked like a relatively normal run until he was twisted around during the tackle.

After Achane went down, he was replaced by Ollie Gordon II. The backup finished the game with 41 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. He added 14 additional yards on three receptions.

Achane is in the final year of his rookie deal. Ahead of the season, he inked a massive 4-year, $64 million deal that takes him through the 2030 season.

Miami will likely have to add some depth at running back. The Dolphins only dressed two running backs for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Jaylen Wright missed the game due to a foot injury and a stinger after not practicing Friday.

The Dolphins do have both Jarquez Hunter and Carlos Washington Jr., who could be elevated from the practice squad. Neither would be a candidate to handle a heavy workload, so it projects to be Gordon's backfield moving forward, even if Miami brings in a veteran presence.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill Provides New Update on Knee Injury Rehab, Top NFL Landing Spots for Star WR's Next Team
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill's return to an NFL field may not be that far away.
articles.body:
Tyreek Hill's return to an NFL field may not be that far away.

Hill, who remained unsigned at the start of the 2026 season as he recovers from the dislocated knee and torn ACL that limited him to just four games in 2025, took to social media Monday and posted that "it's almost time to get off the couch and get to work."

Here is a look at some possible landing spots for Hill:

There was a time when Hill would have been a season-altering addition for any team.

After all, his resume includes a Super Bowl title, five First-Team All-Pro selections, eight Pro Bowl nods, six seasons with more than 1,100 receiving yards and three seasons with double-digit touchdown catches.

He led the NFL in receiving yards (1,799) and touchdown catches (13) during the 2023 campaign, which was his second with the Miami Dolphins after he played for the Chiefs during his first six seasons.

However, potential suitors should not expect him to be that dominant if and when he does return.

Hill is 32 years old and coming off a major injury. He also failed to reach the 1,000-yard mark in 2024 despite playing all 17 games.

But in the right situation, he could still thrive.

And a return to Kansas City may be that right situation.

The 3-0 Chiefs have Kenneth Walker III controlling the running game and Travis Kelce turning back the clock at tight end. Still, Rashee Rice is the only wide receiver with more than 108 receiving yards through the first three games.

Kansas City needs another playmaker at wide receiver, and Hill already has proven chemistry with Patrick Mahomes.

Elsewhere, the Texans are in desperate need of playmakers after an 0-3 start. Nico Collins has been limited to one game with injury, Jayden Higgins is out for the season and Tank Dell is yet to return from the serious knee injury he suffered during the 2024 campaign.

Even when Collins returns, Hill could be a No. 2 option who uses his speed to take advantage of the single coverage he would likely face when sharing the field with his counterpart.

As for the Ravens, they are in a similar situation as the Chiefs with a star running back in Derrick Henry, reliable veteran tight end in Mark Andrews and talented No. 1 wide receiver in Zay Flowers. Yet, much like the Chiefs, they could use a secondary option at wide receiver.

Flowers is the only wide receiver with double-digit catches through three games, so Hill could find immediate playing time for a contender in Baltimore.

Injuries are nothing new at MetLife Stadium, and the New York Giants lost one of their best defenders to a setback during Sunday's 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter reported the belief is pass-rusher Brian Burns suffered a torn ACL during the win.

He is just the latest injury at MetLife Stadium on a long list that includes ACL tears for Malik Nabers, Nick Bosa and Wan'Dale Robinson, as well as an Achilles tear for Aaron Rodgers:

Burns' injury is also another concerning one for a Giants team that already lost quarterback Jaxson Dart to a knee injury. Unlike Burns, Dart did not suffer the injury at MetLife Stadium.

Instead, he was hurt during the team's road loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2.

articles.title: George Kittle Bracing for Fine from NFL After 'Highly Emotional' Celebration in 49ers' Win vs. Cards
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle was dominant during Sunday's 36-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, but his performance will likely cost him some money as well.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle was dominant during Sunday's 36-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, but his performance will likely cost him some money as well.

After his holding call negated a touchdown run from Brock Purdy, Kittle caught a touchdown and celebrated by throwing the ball into the crowd.

"That will probably cost me six grand," he said, per Michael Silver of The Athletic. "What can I say? I was highly emotional."

All that emotion helped him finish with six catches for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 36-30 win. It was more of the same for the tight end who has 12 catches for 174 yards and three scores through three games this season.

San Francisco is 3-0 on the campaign, which will probably make his expected fine easier to deal with for Kittle.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Traded to Giants After Jaxson Dart's Injury, Latest NFL News on Vikings' Return
articles.summary: The New York Giants acquired J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings on Monday.
articles.body:
The New York Giants acquired J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings on Monday.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport, Adam Schefter and Mike Garafolo first reported the news.

Of note, New York head coach John Harbaugh is the brother of McCarthy's college coach, Jim Harbaugh.

This comes after New York quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2. Veteran Jameis Winston has filled in for Dart, leading the Giants to a 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday.

Harbaugh told reporters on Monday that Winston would remain the team's starter even with McCarthy on the roster:

Harbaugh previously made it clear after Sunday's win that he envisioned Winston remaining New York's starting quarterback even if the team added another signal-caller.

"Yes. Yes, I do," Harbaugh said, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan . "Yes, I do."

Acquiring McCarthy gives the Giants more depth at quarterback, and McCarthy even has starting experience. He was, however, behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz on Minnesota's depth chart this year.

McCarthy has been plagued by health woes throughout his first two years in the NFL, as he missed his entire rookie season due to a torn meniscus .

The 23-year-old recovered in time to appear in Minnesota's first two contests in 2025, but eventually suffered a high ankle sprain that caused him to miss five games. He was also absent for a Week 13 clash with the Seattle Seahawks due to a concussion .

McCarthy started slow in 2025, completing 54.1 percent of his passes for 929 yards and six touchdowns compared to 10 interceptions across his first six games.

He progressed as the season continued, though. In his final four appearances, he completed 64.3 percent of his throws for 703 yards and five scores while getting picked off twice.

Still, McCarthy wasn't able to win a positional battle with Murray in training camp this year and entered the regular season as Minnesota's third-string quarterback.

Now, McCarthy will get a fresh start in the Big Apple.

articles.title: Broncos' Hufanga Makes History in Win, Says 'No One Gives Stafford Enough Credit for How Fast He Is'
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford is never going to be on the list of the NFL's fastest quarterbacks, but Denver Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga—who made history Sunday against the veteran—believes the Los Angeles Rams signal-caller deserves more credit for his speed.
articles.body:
Matthew Stafford is never going to be on the list of the NFL's fastest quarterbacks, but Denver Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga—who made history Sunday against the veteran—believes the Los Angeles Rams signal-caller deserves more credit for his speed.

"Man, no one gives Stafford enough credit for how fast he is," Hufanga said when discussing his 66-yard return on a pick-six that required a cut back in Sunday's 30-26 victory over the Rams, per Nick Kosmider of The Athletic.

"That dude, and this is not bragging at all, I've actually been in the same scenario against him in 2022. I saw him, and I ran and said, 'I can keep going (and outrun him),' but somehow as he gets older, he gets faster. I caught the ball and I'm like, 'I don't think I can outrun him (to the sideline),' and that's why I cut back."

Cowboys HC gives himself an F after loss to Ravens

That pick-six gave Denver a 23-19 lead in the fourth quarter, but it wasn't the end of his heroics

Hufanga also intercepted Stafford's pass to the end zone on the final play of the game to preserve the win.

Denver's second-half adjustments were on full display during the interceptions, as the Rams were up 16-0 at halftime but managed just one touchdown the rest of the game. Hufanga explained the secondary recognized it needed to "get sticky" in its coverage to allow the pass-rush to get home, and the Broncos tallied three sacks in the second half.

"Sometimes you get in this habit of, early in a game, you're trying to figure out this offense," Hufanga said. "They do a lot of movements. They're a team that predominantly went into 13 personnel. They're really big and they can still spread the field with the way they do it. Our coach made a great adjustment to just get our eyes in the right spot."

Those adjustments cleared the way for Denver's offense to come back as well.

The Broncos scored 30 points after halftime with Bo Nix throwing for two touchdowns and running for another. The touchdown run in the final minute proved to be the game-winner and propelled the team to a 2-1 record through three games.

And if there are more second-half adjustments in the future like the ones on Sunday, the Broncos figure to once again be AFC contenders after reaching the conference championship game last season.

articles.title: Giants Depth Chart, 2027 NFL Draft Picks, Salary Cap After Surprise J.J. McCarthy Trade with Vikings
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy is on the move for the first time in his NFL career.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy is on the move for the first time in his NFL career.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday the Minnesota Vikings traded the quarterback to the New York Giants in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round draft pick. According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the move saved the Vikings more than $4.6 million in cash and cap space.

Here is a look at New York's updated quarterback depth chart:

🚨 REPORT: GIANTS TRADE FOR J.J. MCCARTHY

McCarthy is joining a Giants team that has $10.9 million in team cap space, per Over The Cap . That team also lost its fifth-round pick in the trade, leaving it with the following 2027 picks:

Sixth Round (Jacksonville Jaguars' pick)

New York has been aggressive in trades including 2027 draft picks outside of just Monday's move.

They acquired a sixth-rounder from the Jaguars for offensive lineman Daniel Faalele but also traded away a fourth-rounder to the Cleveland Browns for Malachi Fields and traded away a seventh-rounder and Darren Waller to the Miami Dolphins.

Attention now turns to the immediate future, though, after adding McCarthy to a quarterback room that will be missing Jaxson Dart for the remainder of the campaign.

New York is still in solid position at 2-1, but it is fair to wonder about the overall ceiling of the team without its starting quarterback. Jameis Winston was unspectacular in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans at 14-of-22 for 118 yards, zero touchdowns and zero interceptions, although he protected the ball and avoided any turnovers.

Sometimes all backup quarterbacks are asked to do is protect the ball, especially when the defense is playing as well as New York did on Sunday.

But Winston is eventually going to have make plays instead of just managing the game if he wants to protect his starting role from McCarthy.

McCarthy, who played for Giants head coach John Harbaugh's brother Jim at Michigan, entered the league as the No. 10 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft but never lived up to elevated expectations in Minnesota.

He missed his rookie season with injury and then completed just 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions last season. He was also demoted to third-string behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz this season, so this move at least gives him a change of scenery and chance to move up a depth chart.

Perhaps Harbaugh will see McCarthy as the quarterback with the higher ceiling and eventually give him a chance as the Giants chase a playoff spot this season. For now, Winston is coming off a win and will look to build momentum in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: B/R Experts Week 4 NFL Power Rankings
articles.summary: We're just three weeks into the 2026 season, but the NFL is already reminding us of an annual tradition.
articles.body:
We're just three weeks into the 2026 season, but the NFL is already reminding us of an annual tradition.

A team (the Las Vegas Raiders) that many expected to be a tomato can is sitting at 3-0 after a wild win in New Orleans. Two teams widely regarded as contenders (the Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers) are winless and reeling. The overwhelming Super Bowl favorite entering the season (the Los Angeles Rams) sits at 1-2 after falling in Denver on Sunday night.

Our preconceptions about contenders and pretenders have been thrown into a blender, but as they do every week Bleacher Report NFL analysts Gary Davenport , Kris Knox , Maurice Moton and Brent Sobleski are here to make sense of that pigskin smoothie by ranking all 32 teams from worst to first.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

Week 3 Result: Lost vs. Kansas City 24-10

The Miami Dolphins have some promising young players, and they kept things interesting with the Kansas City Chiefs for much of Sunday. We're likely to see the Dolphins pull off an upset or two at some point in 2026.

However, the reality is that Miami doesn't have the talent to string together many wins right now. The Dolphins are playing hard for new coach Jeff Hafley, and the wins may still come, but the upcoming schedule is diffuclt, and Miami may have just lost its best offensive player, De'Von Achane, to a knee injury.

"To be honest with you, it does not sound optimistic,' head coach Jeff Hafley said, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . -- Knox

Week 3 Result: Lost at New York Giants 12-7

If there was any doubt that the Tennessee Titans were a bad team, the matter was settled on Sunday in New York.

Granted, the game was short on fireworks on both sides, in part due to the nor'easter that smacked the east coast. But the Titans haven't been moving the ball regardless of the weather. Cam Ward is either unable or unwilling to challenge defenses down the field—the second-year signal-caller averaged five yards an attempt at Met Life. Tennessee entered the week with a bottom-five offense and will leave it the same way.

The team at least finally got first-round rookie Carnell Tate involved offensively. But after back-to-back three-win seasons, 2025 was supposed to be a year of improvement in Nashville.

At this rate, the Titans will be lucky to "improve" to 4-13. And Ward's lack of development has to be unsettling to the team. -- Davenport

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers continue tumbling down our power rankings amid their 0-3 start.

Tampa's offense has struggled to find any semblance of cohesion under new coordinator Zac Robinson, and its defense hasn't done enough to deliver victories. Quarterback Baker Mayfield has struggled—likely while trying too hard to carry the offense—and now appears set to miss time with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand.

It's probably safe to say that Todd Bowles' seat is getting rather warm.

No one is threatening to run away with the NFC South just yet, so there's still time for the Bucs to climb back into their divisional race. However, they'll have to find ways to start stacking some wins soon, or else they could be looking at significant changes before the season is even over. -- Knox

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode

The Los Angeles Chargers are completely lost. An 0-3 start has them swimming for a life raft with one unlikely to appear since the Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs are next on the docket.

Surprisingly, the Chargers' biggest disconnect can be found on offense, where quarterback Justin Herbert isn't executing Mike McDaniel's offensive scheme.

This past offseason, McDaniel's hire was viewed as one of the league's best, because he brought a proven track record as a play-caller. Instead, the Chargers are in disarray, Herbert is playing poorly and the unit ranks among the league's bottom-feeders in total offense. -- Sobleski

Week 3 Result: Lost at San Francisco 36-30

Well, at least the Arizona offense got untracked Sunday in Santa Clara. Jacoby Brissett threw for 280 yards and two scores. Jeremiyah Love tallied 109 total yards. Michael Wilson saw a gaudy 17 targets and caught 11 passes.

For the second time in as many weeks, the Cardinals were cooked defensively by an NFC West foe. The Cardinals allowed 437 yards of offense, 36 points, four passing touchdowns and over six yards a carry on the ground—to a 49ers team that is being blasted by injuries once again.

Things aren't going to get much easier moving forward—a road trip to face the Giants in Week 4 appears winnable. But after that comes home tilts with the Lions and Broncos sandwiched around a trip to Los Angeles to face the Rams. – Davenport

Week 3 Result: Lost at Indianapolis 19-17

The good news is that the Texans are in familiar territory.

The bad news is that familiar territory is up a creek.

This marks the second straight season that the Texans have started 0-3. Last year, they rebounded to make the postseason and won a playoff game. The Texans also started 0-3 and made the playoffs in 2018.

But no team has made the playoffs after an 0-3 start in back-to-back seasons, and right now the Texans do not look the part of a contender—at all.

Houston's offensive line play and rushing attack have been all but non-existent—against a Colts defense that entered Week 3 with the AFC's worst defense, the Texans had 70 rushing yards and averaged less than 3.5 yards per carry. C.J. Stroud had his worst game of the season throwing the ball in Indianapolis.

Houston's defense can't do it all—and right now the offense isn't doing much. – Davenport

The New York Jets have been surprisingly competitive through the first three weeks. While the Detroit Lions pulled away from them on Sunday, the Jets won their opener and probably should have outlasted the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.

New York is developing a solid young core, and it's beginning to look like Aaron Glenn might be the right coach for this team after all. His first season with the franchise didn't go well, but he's shown this season that he can field a balanced and effective football team.

Equipped with three 2027 first-round picks, the Jets are likely laying the foundation for a quarterback to be drafted next April. That doesn't mean they aren't a team that must be taken seriously right now, because they are—though losing Breece Hall to a thigh injury hurts them in the short term. -- Knox

What a difference having a competent quarterback makes.

Michael Penix Jr. made his 2026 debut on Thursday night, and the Atlanta Falcons immediately transformed from being a hapless NFC afterthought to looking like a potential playoff team. Penix sparked the passing game and forged a nearly unstoppable connection with Drake London (9 catches, 194 yards). That helped open up the ground game and unlocked Bijan Robinson (194 rushing yards, 2 TDs).

Atlanta's defense also played splendidly in Week 3, unshackled from the burden of having to carry an inept offense. After crafting a short-week game plan that the Green Bay Packers were never able to counter, even head coach Kevin Stefanski came away looking good.

It was a much-needed get-right game for the Falcons. Only time will tell, though, whether they're ready to reenter the playoff conversation or if the Packers are just not good this year. -- Knox

The Washington Commanders have their signature win of the season—a victory over the reigning Super Bowl champions with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota under center. The Commanders offense moved the ball consistently against arguably the league's best defense, and Mariota sealed the win on a scramble for a first down.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could be back within three weeks. After Mariota's Week 3 performance, the Commanders don't need to rush Daniels back; their offense fared well without him in the short term. -- Moton

Sunday's game between the Texans and Colts featured two teams trying not to let the season get away from them. The Colts prevailed.

But that doesn't make them a playoff contender. Or a good team.

To Indy's credit, the defense played its best game of the year—although that may have had more to do with the Houston offense than the Colts defense. It wasn't pretty, but the Indianapolis offense found ways to grind out points against an excellent Houston defense.

In the NFL, you take wins any way you can get them—especially at 0-2.

The next month will be pivotal for the Colts—a four-game stretch against the Commanders, Steelers, Titans and Vikings. If the Colts want to claw back into the AFC South hunt, they need to figure out a way to eke out three wins before opening November against the Jaguars in Jacksonville. -- Davenport

Matt LaFleur has had a good run as the Green Bay Packers' head coach and offensive play-caller. Apparently, it ended when this season began.

Right now, the Packers lack a functional offense. The running game is non-existent. In fact, Green Bay's rushing offense averages just under 49 yards per contest. No other team averages fewer than 81 yards.

Plus, injuries to the team's offensive line makes life more difficult on everyone. The group can't hold up in protection. This issue shouldn't come as a surprise after seeing Thursday's lineup, where the team's front five consisted of four new starters, considering Jordan Morgan moved to left tackle this season and a pair of injuries tested Green Bay's depth. -- Sobleski

Through three weeks, we don't have a clear idea of who the Carolina Panthers are in 2026. They racked up 37 points in Week 1 while still losing by double digits. In Week 2, they embarrassed the NFC South rival Atlanta Falcons 34-3. Looking to get to 2-1 against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, the Panthers fell flat.

Quarterback Bryce Young had his worst game of the season in Week 3, and the Panthers mustered a season-low scoring total as a result. While the defense spent much of the game letting the Browns shoot themselves in the foot offensively, it imploded on Cleveland's go-ahead touchdown drive late in the fourth quarter.

Week 3 may have simply been a flukey performance on the road, or these Panthers may not be much different than last year's squad—a largely average team that only occasionally put together a complete performance. Carolina did win the NFC South in 2025, but it doesn't feel like 8-9 will be enough to take the division this year. -- Knox

The Cleveland Browns are racking up wins against the NFC South, beating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Carolina Panthers by close margins. Deshaun Watson only completed about half of his pass attempts in the previous outing, but he's doing enough to lead the Browns to victories, throwing two touchdown passes without an interception in back-to-back games.

We'll see how Cleveland handles a little success in a division matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers coming up on a short week. -- Moton

It's fitting that the New York Giants won a gritty game in the rain because they must be willing to grind through games and play physical football to win.

Without quarterback Jaxson Dart, who's out for the season, the Giants will likely move the ball with a heavy dose of bruising running backs Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris, which will limit quarterback Jameis Winston's turnovers. Or the Giants could eventually turn to former first-round pick J.J. McCarthy, who the G-Men acquired in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings Monday.

It's not an appealing winning formula with Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely on the field, but it could be effective for this team. -- Moton

The Super Bowl hangover is in full effect for the New England Patriots, who have looked and played almost nothing like last year's squad. Drake Maye has been even more mistake-prone than he was as a rookie and has actively cost the Patriots games.

Through three weeks, Maye has completed a career-worst 63.8 percent of his passes for one touchdown, six interceptions, and a 58.6 quarterback rating. He has also lost a fumble.

There's no guarantee that New England can get back on a playoff trajectory simply by settling in Maye, either. The defense has been solid overall but not quite disruptive enough to take over games. The Buffalo Bills are up next, and if the Patriots can't steal one in Week 4, it could be time for them to panic. -- Knox

Although it sounds like a broken record with this team, the Dallas Cowboys defense is a liability. In Rio de Janeiro, defensive coordinator Christian Parker set up his unit for failure, leaving the middle of the field open for Lamar Jackson to connect with Zay Flowers on a 27-yard completion before Tyler Loop kicked a 56-yard game-winning field goal.

Dallas has allowed nearly 400 total yards in all three of its games. Parker needs to make overall and situational adjustments on his side of the ball. -- Moton

Right now, the Chicago Bears are trying to weather the storm.

With Caleb Williams (hamstring) and Tyson Bagent (concussion) both banged up, the Bears will be forced to turn to veteran journeyman Case Keenum at quarterback Monday night against the Eagles.

And with the Vikings at 3-0, the Bears can't afford to fall too far off the pace in the NFC North. -- Sobleski

New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough had played like a viable MVP candidate through most of the first three weeks. Unfortunately, he had a critical fourth-quarter interception on Sunday that led to a lead-extending Las Vegas Raiders touchdown, and he had another fumble after that.

The Saints are just good enough that they can beat very good teams when Shough is playing nearly flawless football. However, they're not good enough to consistently hang with playoff-caliber teams—and Las Vegas may just be one of those this season—when Shough makes multiple mistakes.

New Orleans is still trying to find some rhythm in its ground game and more consistency from a defense that is allowing just over 27 points per game.

If the Saints can do those things, they can make a run at their first NFC South title since 2020. Until then, they must be considered fringe contenders at best. -- Knox

Between these AFC North rivals, four of the last six matchups were high-scoring battles. The Bengals came up short in this one, and their defense took a big step back after forcing four turnovers in Week 1 and holding the Houston Texans to six points last week.

Cincinnati's defense still has weak spots in coverage, as it allowed Aaron Rodgers to throw for 292 yards and three touchdowns, though it picked him off once. The Bengals are a few spots outside of our top 10, which feels right for them. -- Moton

The Pittsburgh Steelers entered Week 3 averaging the fewest yards per play (3.8). Offensively, they woke up to match scoring drives and outduel the Cincinnati Bengals.

In Week 3, Aaron Rodgers looked like an NBA point guard on the field, logging a completion to nine different pass-catchers, with touchdown throws to DK Metcalf, Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek. Perhaps Pittsburgh needed this performance to establish its offensive rhythm. -- Moton

Week 3 Result: Won vs. New York Jets 31-24

The Detroit Lions responded after a disappointing loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thursday Night Football . Granted, Sunday's victory came at the expense of the New York Jets, who aren't on Buffalo's level. However, the Lions took care of business. Specifically, the Lions showed some defensive improvement.

Dan Campbell's squad will be able to move the ball, because the Lions feature too much offensive talent and quarterback Jared Goff is the perfect facilitator within their scheme. The defense hasn't held up its end of the bargain, though.

Specifically, Detroit surrendered 915 yards through the first two weeks of play. For those keeping track, that's nearly 460 yards on average. The Jets managed a more respectable 335 yards. The Lions were particularly stingy at the point of attack by allowing only 58 rushing yards. With Geno Smith's 12 yards taken out of the equation, Breece Hall and Braelon Allen averaged a measly 2.7 yards per carry. -- Sobleski

At 3-0, the Las Vegas Raiders have already matched their entire win total from last season. It's amazing how different a team can look thanks to organizational competency. It's only the second time since 2002 this franchise opened a season with three straight wins.

Are the Raiders legit, though? Obviously, the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers aren't good. The New Orleans Saints are highly competitive, but Kellen Moore's squad has found ways to lose during his time as head coach. Next week's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs will provide a true test.

Las Vegas should be ready for its upcoming matchup now that Brock Bowers is back. Much like Travis Kelce, Bowers isn't an ordinary tight end. He's the Raiders' No. 1 target, as evidenced by 10 catches for 116 yards upon his return to the lineup. -- Sobleski

The Los Angeles Rams cannot catch a break.

This is a team whose prized offseason acquisition is out indefinitely after knee surgery. Whose No. 1 wide receiver has missed the last two games with an ambiguous abdominal injury.

In Denver Sunday night, the Rams squandered a 16-0 lead and lost a game they should have won despite those personnel losses. The phantom DPI call on Denver's game-winning drive was a factor, sure. But so was a second half where the Rams defense took a nap to the tune of 30 points allowed.

It's not time to hit the big red panic button. In the first half, the Rams looked the part of the team so many expected them to be this year. 1-2 isn't the end of the world.

But it is time to worry. The Rams aren't shaking off the injuries like their rivals in San Francisco. Said injuries continue to mount. The schedule is brutal, with the Eagles and Bills next.

Again, the Rams can't catch a break. -- Davenport

Last week, Knox wrote that Sunday's visit from the defending AFC champions, "will speak volumes about how seriously we should take the Jaguars as AFC contenders."

Knox was absolutely right—because the Jaguars dropped a set of encyclopedias on the New England Patriots Sunday.

For the second time in as many home games this year, the Jaguars completely dominated their opponent. Trevor Lawrence didn't have a big day yardage-wise, but he threw three touchdown passes. Jacksonville averaged 4.6 yards a carry and found paydirt twice on the ground. The Jags converted eight of 12 third downs. And the team forced three turnovers.

There is zero question that the Jaguars are the best team in the AFC South. With a trip to Cincinnati and a visit from the Eagles next up, the Jaguars have an opportunity to stake their claim as a legit Super Bowl contender as well. -- Davenport

Week 3 Result: Won at Dallas 34-31 (Brazil)

The Baltimore Ravens played to win—not for overtime in Rio de Janeiro, and their aggressive approach paid off. After the Ravens advanced the ball to their own 35-yard line off a touchback, Lamar Jackson threw a 27-yard dart to Zay Flowers, which set up Tyler Loop's 56-yard game-winning field goal.

In a critical moment, the Ravens were the better team. Too many times under the previous coaching regime, they fell apart in those scenarios. It's an early sign of progress under first-year head coach Jesse Minter. -- Moton

The Minnesota Vikings understand the exact blueprint for them to be successful, even if it's not pretty. Brian Flores is going to bring more pressure than any other defensive play-caller and dictate games. The approach is simple yet effective.

Kyler Murray's return to the lineup didn't exactly jumpstart Minnesota's offense. The Vikings' 230 yards were fewer than the team managed during the previous two weeks with Carson Wentz at the helm.

Maybe Murray shows more once he gets comfortable in Kevin O'Connell's offense. As for now, Minnesota will blitz, blitz and blitz some more to ensure they're in a position to win every game possible. -- Sobleski

Week 3 Result: Won vs. Los Angeles Rams 30-26

The Denver Broncos continually find ways to win despite getting out of the gate slowly. They did so again against the Los Angeles Rams. Bo Nix and Co. trailed 16-0 at halftime after mustering only 67 yards. Yet, these horses know how to close down the stretch.

Denver scored 30 second-half points to beat the Rams. It did so through a combination of its offense getting on track, while leaning on an opportunistic defense.

At some point, this formula will backfire. The Broncos have continually gotten away with it for over a year now. For whatever reason, Nix doesn't play well until after halftime. If head coach Sean Payton can figure out how to get his team started quickly, the Broncos would be the NFL's toughest team to beat. -- Sobleski

There are no "gimme" wins in the NFL. Yes, the Seattle Seahawks had looked as good as any team in the NFL over the first two weeks of the season. The winless Commanders, on the other hand, were rolling out a backup quarterback in Marcus Mariota.

But while Sam Darnold threw for 379 yards and four scores in his return from injury, he also threw a pair of costly interceptions—one of which was a pick-six. A third turnover set Washington up with a short field. The Seahawks couldn't run the ball at all—less than 50 yards and 2.4 yards per carry. And despite outgaining the Commanders by almost 200 yards, Seattle came up short on the scoreboard.

Now the Seahawks will host a desperate Chargers team before a brutal three-game stretch.

They need to flush this stinker and get back to work. -- Davenport

The Philadelphia Eagles will face third-string quarterback Case Keenum in the Monday Night Football matchup, but they shouldn't take the Chicago Bears lightly.

The Eagles' defense has been susceptible to the run, giving up an average of 127 rushing yards in two games. Philadelphia will likely spend a lot of the night tackling running backs D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai. -- Moton

The Kansas City Chiefs went to Miami and handled business against an inferior opponent. It shouldn't be surprising that quarterback Patrick Mahomes wasn't entirely thrilled with the performance despite a two-score victory.

The Chiefs approach is evolving, though. Kansas City isn't the same team that won back-to-back Super Bowls a few years ago. Mahomes isn't forced to do everything as part of the team's current offense.

Kenneth Walker III is as much the focal point as the two-time NFL MVP. Kansas City relies more on the play-action passing game than any other team. Mahomes has feasted when defenses start to cheat up in hopes of slowing Walker. This version of KC's offense will be extremely difficult to stop as it progresses. -- Sobleski

49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan might be a sorcerer.

It seemingly doesn't matter how many players get hurt in San Francisco. The team just keeps winning. Sunday against the Redbirds, the Niners ended the game short their best edge-rusher in Nick Bosa and watched top wideout Mike Evans get carted off the field with a rib injury.

Actually, while Shanahan deserves a ton of credit for coaching up his guys, we need to give Brock Purdy his flowers as one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Purdy continued his stellar start to the season—297 passing yards, four touchdowns and a passer rating north of 130.

"Mr. Irrelevant" is anything but. Per ESPN , Purdy tied Steve Young's 49ers team record for most touchdown passes in the first three games of a season. The Niners haven't scored this many points in their first three games since 1998.

With Young and some guy named Jerry Rice. -- Davenport

The Buffalo Bills got to 3-0 on Sunday, and they may still be one of the teams to beat in the AFC. However, Buffalo's undefeated start to the season has included some concerns.

The Bills' defense still seems average at best, which is a significant problem when Josh Allen fails to take care of the football. And while Allen has statistically been a viable early MVP candidate, his ball security has left something to be desired.

Buffalo would have dropped its opener had Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter not dropped the late pass that Allen threw right to him. Allen's three turnovers against the Chargers left the Bills flirting with an upset loss.

3-0 is 3-0, and there aren't many quarterbacks a team would rather carry into the postseason. However, we may not know if this incarnation of the Bills is any better than last year's unit until we actually reach January. -- Knox

articles.title: Tom Brady Lost Nearly 20 Lbs. as Gisele Bündchen Marriage Unraveled, New Book Claims: ‘Looked Like a Cancer Patient’
articles.summary: “His cheekbones had freaking cheekbones,” one former coach said
articles.body:
Tom Brady lost nearly 20 pounds, leading to concern from his teammates and coaches, as his marriage to Gisele Bündchen was ending in 2022

Bruce Arians said Brady "looked like a cancer patient with really good hair" in a new book about the quarterback

Brady "just seemed miserable" and was "so stressed," former coaches recalled

Tom Brady was "so stressed" from marital challenges with Gisele Bündchen that he lost nearly 20 pounds before his final NFL season in 2022, according to a new book about the former quarterback.

In an excerpt from Lars Anderson's book, Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness, obtained by PEOPLE, the author said Brady's former Tampa Bay Buccaneers teammates "worried that he was ill" when he reported to training camp for his final season because he had lost so much weight.

Anderson spoke to former Buccaneers head coach Bruce Arians, who said, "It was very clear that the reason for the weight loss was the stress from the personal issues he was dealing with," and said the quarterback "looked like a cancer patient with really good hair."

"But his problems were clearly impacting his physical well-being," Arians said in the book, describing Brady as someone who "prides himself on his physical condition," which made the NFL star's weight loss "jarring" for those who knew him. "And he just seemed miserable, not even close to the Tom we all loved. He was so stressed."

Arians said the Buccaneers locker room "knew about his marital problems, and it wasn't difficult to put the two together," in Anderson's book.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

Another former Buccaneers coach told Anderson, "His cheekbones had freaking cheekbones."

A third member of the organization recalled that Brady "never smiled" and "wasn't himself from the moment he showed up for training camp."

Reps for Brady and Bündchen did not immediately return PEOPLE's request for comment on Monday, Sept. 28.

Anderson's book also detailed Brady's alleged last-ditch effort to save his marriage to Bündchen, with whom he shares Benjamin Rein and Vivian Lake . Brady shares son John "Jack" Edward Thomas with his ex-girlfriend, actress Bridget Moynahan .

Bündchen and her now-husband, Joaquim Valente, welcomed their first baby together, a boy , in February 2025.

Bündchen, 46, and Brady announced they were separating shortly before their divorce was finalized in October 2022.

On an episode of The Herd with Colin Cowherd earlier this year, Brady, now 49, opened up about how his divorce affected his final NFL season.

"My last season was tough," he confessed. "I was going through, I had a lot of, you know, a personal family issue," he continued, seemingly in reference to his and Bündchen's divorce. "And it was a challenge, and it was very … it just took a lot out of me in terms of, you know, my ability to play."

Brady retired from the NFL in 2023 and has since shifted into broadcasting. He is in his third season working the top NFL booth at Fox.

articles.title: Giants made the one QB trade that offered hope, even if it doesn't guarantee anything
articles.summary: Trading for McCarthy makes some short- and long-term success, even if it's still not guaranteed to work.
articles.body:
When news broke that Jaxson Dart was done for the season and the New York Giants were shopping for quarterback help , it was hard not to think: Good luck .

Quarterbacks don't grow on trees. Smart teams don't let good ones out of the building often, at least not for cheap.

But there was one available option to the Giants , trading for J.J. McCarthy , that at least offered a glimmer of hope. Will it work? That remains a stretch, based on how McCarthy has played.

Yet it at least has a chance to work, which is likely better than you can say about the other options the Giants had. Most of them were short-term rentals. Most of them were older and more experienced, but there was a reason they were either unemployed or available by trade.

McCarthy's circumstances are unique. He's a recent high first-round draft pick who fell out of favor with the Minnesota Vikings , a club quite willing to move on from him. The cost (a 2027 fifth-rounder) was pretty indicative of that, selling for quarters on the dollar after a little more than two years of him being in the building.

Somehow, McCarthy fell from competing for the Vikings' starting job in mid-August to being their QB3 by early September. It was telling that Carson Wentz , not McCarthy, was Kyler Murray 's backup when he was knocked out of Minnesota's Week 1 game. McCarthy's problems weren't all football-related, either. He'd clearly lost the trust of the Vikings' coaching staff, one that has previously cobbled together functional offenses with less-credentialed QBs.

That's a reminder of where McCarthy was prior to the trade: the third QB option on a team that ranks last in the NFL in total yards, pass yards and first downs. It should also serve as a warning for any Giants fans counting on this saving their season.

Granted, the bar is low for the post-Dart Giants. Jameis Winston struggled badly against the Rams after Dart was injured and was passable at best Sunday in a close-shave win over the Titans at home . Four field goals and 238 yards of offense might work vs. Tennessee , but it's probably not going to cut it much going forward, with the toughest part of the Giants' schedule upcoming.

McCarthy was the one trade option that made sense

There were plenty of dots to connect between McCarthy and the Giants, so this is far from a shocking trade. He played for Jim Harbaugh at Michigan and now gets brother John; this is not the first time they've swapped players, and even coaches. The Giants also did ample background work on McCarthy prior to the 2024 NFL Draft and appeared to like him.

They clearly like something about McCarthy now, even if his situation has dramatically changed. One, he was cheap. Two, he's a young QB at age 23 — four months older than Dart — who's had only 10 starts to show himself. The Giants said they wanted to add an "experienced" quarterback, so it remains to be seen if this is the experience level they were actually seeking, but this trade also has some potential long-term benefits.

Yes, McCarthy is being brought in to help this season. There was a real question how long they could have stuck with Winston, and they were one hit away from playing Jake Haener . So you can bet the Giants will throw the kitchen sink at McCarthy and see how he responds. The Giants have games against the Cardinals, Commanders and Texans prior to the Week 8 bye. The next month will tell us a lot about how quickly the Giants plan to bring McCarthy into the fold.

But the trade also offers a bit of long-term insurance. Dart will have missed 17 of 34 games with injury by season's end. A concussion and evalutions over suspected head injuries were a major Year 1 storyline, and the knee has been the headline for Year 2. Even with aggressive rehab, he still could be limited early next offseason, and the Giants likely knew they need better contingency plans.

Can McCarthy provide that? Maybe. The results to this point are what they are. The Giants will take a little ugly if McCarthy can deliver some victories, even if they look as sluggish as the one Winston helped deliver Sunday. But they clearly want to see improvement on what he did with the Vikings, and that means getting better with Giants offensive personnel that is arguably no more or less impressive than what Minnesota has.

If McCarthy plays well enough, he could be in the Giants' 2027 mix. Dart remains the franchise QB until proven otherwise, and McCarthy's arrival could complicate matters down the road. Some trades have costs that go beyond draft-pick compensation and salary, and this is one of them. Will Dart feel threatened by McCarthy's arrival? It'll be interesting to hear what the Giants say about this and whether they consulted Dart before making the trade.

The Giants inherit a looming decision next summer on McCarthy's fifth-year option, which also would be tough to green light even if McCarthy plays well. For now, they can afford McCarthy's first-round salary this year and next, even if, interestingly enough, he'll make a shade more money than Dart will.

Those are more trivial details for now. The bottom line is that the Giants are gambling on McCarthy's talent and intangibles, even if there might be a lot to clean up — those late eyes and forced balls we've seen too much of speak for themselves. Coaching him up for starter-level duty will require some serious fast-tracking from this staff.

There were more immediately ready options available that didn't require picks to be traded — hired-gun free-agent quarterbacks who have previously joined other teams in a pinch and readied themselves for quick action. No one would have blamed the Giants if they went out and signed Jimmy Garoppolo or Brandon Allen or a similar-ilk QB.

Trading for McCarthy was a break from that strategy. It appears the Giants are as worried about tomorrow as they are about today. The problem? This trade doesn't guarantee that either concern will be fully addressed. That is the risk, even for such a relatively low-cost trade.

The Washington Commanders shouldn't have been able to knock off the Seattle Seahawks without Jayden Daniels in the lineup. Marcus Mariota and Co. did.
