articles.title: Dillon Thieneman’s first NFL interception couldn’t have come at a better time
articles.summary: Chicago Bears rookie Dillon Thieneman just came up big. The first-round safety’s first career interception couldn’t have come on a more clutch occasion: swip...
articles.body:
Chicago Bears rookie Dillon Thieneman just came up big.

The first-round safety's first career interception couldn't have come on a more clutch occasion: swiping Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Andy Dalton in the red zone to take away a potential touchdown and maintain the Bears' 7-0 lead in the second quarter.

(In case you're wondering, starting quarterback Jalen Hurts was momentarily out of the game while being evaluated for a possible concussion after a late hit by linebacker D'Marco Jackson, which is why Dalton, the former Bears quarterback , was in the game.)

What a moment, on Monday Night Football, to make such a huge play.

The young safety has quietly been one of the Bears' most consistent players early in the season, which is simultaneously good and concerning. (Your safety shouldn't be your leading tackler coming into Week 3 in an ideal world.) Still, it's nice to know the guy brought in to be an immediate difference-maker has proven to be just that.

And now, he's checked off a big box on his resume: "first career interception." Thankfully, Dalton made it easy for him.

The nice part: this pick wasn't just "a meatball sub," in the words of Tom Brady from last week. It also helped the Bears maintain a lead not many people expected them to have at this point against the Eagles with Keenum at quarterback. In fact, funnily enough, it stole points off the board for the Eagles after the Bears had failed on 4th and goal with a chance to go up two touchdowns.

As a safety, Thieneman probably won't top too many people's lists for Defensive Rookie of the Year, especially if the Bears continue being a largely "mid" defense.

But make no mistake: so far, the youngin has done his job on the back end of the defense.

Here's to many more interceptions to come.

articles.title: Chicago Bears S Dillon Thieneman snags first NFL interception
articles.summary: Former Oregon safety Dillon Thieneman made his first NFL interception on Monday Night Football for the Chicago Bears against the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
What a week for former Oregon Ducks in the NFL.

After a Sunday full of game-winning plays by former Ducks across the league and an incredible performance by Marcus Mariota to knock off the reigning Super Bowl champions, the success continued on Monday night in prime-time action.

Rookie safety Dillon Thieneman snagged his first NFL interception on Monday Night Football as the Chicago Bears took on the Philadelphia Eagles . The former Duck was a first-round pick by the Bears and has quickly become a leader for the defense in Chicago.

On a third-down pass at the goal line, Thieneman stepped in front of a pass from Eagles quarterback Andy Dalton to make an interception, denying Philadelphia an opportunity to tie the game in the second quarter. Thieneman was quite active in the early portion of the game, leading the Bears defense with five tackles and a pass deflection before making the turnover.

Occasionally, it can take time for a rookie defender to settle into a role. However, Thieneman has been leaned on heavily from the start, and he's already looking like a steal in the back end of the first round. Thieneman led the Bears with 17 tackles and a pair of deflections entering Monday night.

In his lone season with the Ducks, Thieneman made 92 tackles from his safety position, while also snagging two interceptions and making five pass breakups. Before his time at Oregon, Thieneman racked up 210 tackles and six interceptions over two seasons at Purdue.

Thieneman has been one of Oregon's standouts from the 2026 NFL Draft, with tight end Kenyon Sadiq and linebacker Bryce Boettcher also making plenty of plays with their respective teams early in the NFL season. On a Bears defense that was in desperate need of help in the secondary, Thieneman's interception figures to be the first of many in his NFL career.

articles.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts leaves game vs. Bears briefly after hard hit out of bounds, evaluated for concussion
articles.summary: Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson drilled Jalen Hurts hard out of bounds on Monday night.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was taken out of their game against the Chicago Bears briefly on Monday night after taking a hard hit out of bounds.

Hurts appeared to be fine after the hit, which drew an unnecessary roughness penalty at Soldier Field, but officials still took him out of the game and sent him to the blue medial tent to get evaluated for a concussion.

Hurts was scrambling to the right side midway through the second quarter and made it right to the first down marker when Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson drilled him hard in the shoulder. Hurts had just barely stepped out of bounds before Jackson got to him, and he went down hard.

Hurts remained down on the ground briefly, but eventually got up and walked back onto the field on his own. Jackson was called for a penalty, but it was negated by an earlier hold on the Eagles.

While Hurts got up on his own and appeared fine, officials still pulled him out to check him for a concussion.

Andy Dalton came in to replace Hurts for the rest of the drive. Though they were just yards away from the end zone, the Bears stuffed the Eagles twice and then intercepted Dalton to force a turnover and maintain their lead.

Hurts, meanwhile, looked livid that he wasn't able to go back into the game right away.

While there's no guarantee that Hurts would have finished off that drive with a touchdown, the hard hit out of bounds absolutely made things much more complicated for the Eagles' offense in the moment.

"Obviously frustrating, but the doctors have to do their job," Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said on ESPN at halftime. "They have to protect these guys. We had a hit on the sidelines that they looked at, and that's the way it goes."

Jalen Hurts returns, mounts TD drive immediately

Hurts was eventually cleared by team doctors and the independent evaluator, and he returned to the field on the next drive. But the Bears made it all the way down the field after the interception and extended their lead with a 29-yard field goal from Cairo Santos .

Once given the ball again, Hurts wasted no time proving to Eagles fans that he was OK. He led the Eagles on a very quick touchdown drive, thanks in part to a huge 30-yard pass to DeVonta Smith . Hurts then capped the drive off with a one-yard touchdown run himself right as time expired. He just barely got the snap off, too.

Hurts went 10-of-13 for 111 yards in the first half. The final touchdown cut the Bears' lead to just three points at the break.

This post will be updated with more information shortly.

articles.title: Eagles vs. Bears, Live Updates: Jalen Hurts scores last-gasp TD to cut lead before halftime
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles take on the Chicago Bears on Monday night at Soldier Field. Follow for updates from the Week 3 showdown.
articles.body:
CHICAGO — Greetings from the press box at Soldier Field, where the Philadelphia Eagles will battle the Chicago Bears on "Monday Night Football."

Jalen Hurts and the Eagles are 2-0 after wins over the Commanders and Titans to open the season.

The Bears , meanwhile, are 1-1. They hung 59 points on the Panthers in Week 1 but lost to the Vikings, 9-3, in Week 2.

Chicago are without quarterback Caleb Williams , who injured his hamstring last week. And with backup Tyson Bagent coming back from a concussion, the Bears will start 38-year-old third-stringer Case Keenum .

The Eagles have a favorable history against Keenum . We'll see if they can get to the veteran and defend the run better than they did in last year's Black Friday loss to the Bears.

Zach Ertz is back . Jonathan Greenard is set to make his Eagles debut. Plenty to keep an eye on tonight.

Stay here for updates throughout the game from Chicago.

Wow, what a sequence. Jalen Hurts orchestrated an exhilarating two-minute drill to cut the lead before halftime.

The Eagles, curiously, dialed up screen pass with no timeouts to bring it down to the 1-yard line. Hurts looked like he was going to spike it and set up a field goal as time was expiring. Instead, Hurts barely got the snap off and sneaked his way into the end zone as the clock hit zero.

Huge stuff from Hurts. And incredible catch by DeVonta Smith to help set it all up.

The Eagles could be leading this game if not for a few major penalties. They could also be losing by a lot more. Down three and getting the ball to start the second half, they'll take it.

Case Keenum's performance so far really puts the Eagles' shoddy QB2 situation into perspective. The 38-year-old third-stringer is dicing up the Eagles' safeties. This time, completions of 25, 22, 15 and 13 yards guided the Bears on a scoring drive, capped by a 29-yard field goal.

A whole lot happened on a drive that yielded zero points for the Eagles. Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley engineered a 95-yard drive on the doorstep of the Bears' end zone.

But a late hit by the Bears forced Hurts to be evaluated for a concussion. Andy Dalton came in and threw a pick on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line.

Moments after the interception, Hurts emerged from the blue medical tent and was cleared to return. A brutal sequence for the Eagles.

The Eagles' defense stood tall. After a Jalen Carter tackle for loss, the Bears faced a fourth-and-goal from the 3-yard line. Chicago coach Ben Johnson decided to go for it instead of taking the field. Not a wise choice. Also not wise? Targeting Quinyon Mitchell . The All-Pro's PBU cements a big stand.

The Eagles' offense can't stop making mistakes. Jalen Hurts short-armed throw in the flat to Saquon Barkley, who had a lot of green ahead of him. Tyler Steen had an unnecessary holding penalty to wipe out a long Barkley run. Then, Tank Bigsby fumbled on a second-and-20 checkdown to gift the Bears the ball at Philadelphia's 15-yard line.

Schematically, I like what Sean Mannion is doing so far. His players are letting him down from an execution standpoint.

That was a less than ideal start for the Eagles' defense — and a masterful opening drive by Bears head coach and play-caller Ben Johnson.

Chicago's misdirection and run game cooked Vic Fangio's unit, marching on an 11-play, 66-yard touchdown drive.

Reminiscent of last year's Black Friday blitz by the Bears.

TV: ESPN (Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, Lisa Salters, Laura Rutledge)
